proposal: The Mandate recommends that DHS lift limits on CBP publishing detailed border enforcement data and issue a regulation requiring regular, timely public data free of White House and DHS leadership review. It also recommends combining Border Patrol with Air and Marine Operations and the Office of Trade with the Office of Field Operations, having CBP turn aliens over to ICE and issue Notices to Appear only in limited humanitarian cases, and eliminating Notices to Report altogether (an item repeated in the executive order list on page 151).

status_summary: Executive Order 14165 (signed 2025-01-20), section 5, directs DHS to detain apprehended people until removal and to issue guidance or rules ending catch-and-release, and a CBP memo of the same date, known through a tracking site's summary of an image, limits parole to named senior officials with written justification. A January 2025 directive to Border Patrol to stop issuing Notices to Appear with release, except generally for medical reasons, was reported but not read. A senator's letter of 2025-02-25 says Notices to Report are no longer in operation and were set aside by a federal court in 2023, before this period. CBP's website continues to publish encounter data, but no regulation requiring publication free of leadership review, and no merger of Border Patrol with Air and Marine Operations or of Trade with Field Operations, was found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14165 was signed; section 5 directs the Secretary of Homeland Security to detain apprehended people to the fullest extent of the law until removal and to issue guidance or propose rules ending catch-and-release.

title: CBP: publish enforcement data, limit Notices to Appear, merge Border Patrol and air units
uncertainties: The CBP catch-and-release memo was not read as text; the tracking page summarizes an image of it, and the January 2025 Notice to Appear directive rests on a social media post and news reports summarized by the same tracking site, so neither is a timeline event. Executive Order 14165 was read on federalregister.gov by the researcher and again in review (2026-10-18); it has no Notice to Appear, Notice to Report, data-publication or component-merger provision. The senator's letter says Notices to Report are no longer in operation and cites a 2023 federal court decision setting the related release policies aside; the elimination therefore predates this period and is not credited. The CBP encounters page prints no date and shows only that data continue to be published, with a caveat that figures change with corrections; it does not show whether leadership review changed. Federal Register API queries since 2025-01-20 for CBP with notice to appear (researcher: eleven unrelated results) and for notices to report (review: 0 results), and a web search for a Border Patrol and Air and Marine Operations or Trade and Field Operations merger, found no rule or reorganization document.
